text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past interactions as broad interest signals, often extending them beyond the specific experience or practical need users currently want to pursue.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they continue a clearly repeated preference, such as a musical artist, holiday theme, or mounting task.",
    "Complementary items appeal when they support an established activity or add a useful function to equipment users already own."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with stronger matches to recent mood, specific tasks, and sustained preferences.",
    "Specialized supplies and upgrades assume equipment, compatibility, or replacement needs that interaction histories do not establish.",
    "Similar products are treated as useful next purchases even when recent purchases have already satisfied the underlying need."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category membership, shared terminology, and general workshop or electronics associations produce weak personal matches.",
    "Familiar eras, collection labels, and ecosystem membership substitute for specific artist, functional, or experiential connections."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent interactions and repeated narrow preferences help distinguish current intent from older, broader interests.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, required equipment, and the next plausible task determine whether related products have immediate utility.",
    "Unidentified items and isolated interactions provide limited evidence of preference; uncertainty does not establish dislike."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The top recommendations too often offer general relevance without a sufficiently supported reason to choose the item now, leaving too few matches to current intent and practical needs.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked recommendations users would choose, distinguishing clear matches from uncertain relevance and explicit mismatches.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked items requiring unsupported equipment, incompatible specifications, or already satisfied needs.",
    "The frequency with which broad associations outrank items connected to recent behavior, repeated specific preferences, or a supported complementary task."
  ]
}
